To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ocular counter rotation induced by slanted structures is mainly due to the vestibular system, and that in the case of loss of vestibular input, this rotation is replaced by a combination of other sensory inputs, which are not very precise.

the ocular rotation and the perception of the horizontal are mainly determined by the vestibular system and that the visual and somatosensory systems are not able to substitute for vestibular information.

Ocular counter rotation (OCR) in healthy subjects is mainly due to stimulation of the otolith organs and only to a small extent due to slanted visual structures, whereas in subjects without vestibular function OCR is induced by stimulation of visual and/or somatosensory modalities."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the vestibular system contributes to the perception of the horizontal.
the question of whether the vestibulo-ocular reflex is the main factor in the perception of horizontal orientation in the absence of a gravitational reference signal.
the interaction of different sensory modalities in the perception of the subjective horizontal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in healthy subjects, the ocular counter rotation is mainly induced by otolith stimulation, whereas in patients with loss of vestibular input, the ocular (counter) rotation is mainly induced through the visual and somatosensory system.
the vestibular system is the main source of information for the orientation of the head and eyes.
the vestibular function is of major importance for the perception of the horizontal and the maintenance of ocular rotation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in patients without labyrinth function the ocular system is able to compensate for the loss of otolith information, and the vestibular information is substituted by visual and somatosensory signals.
in healthy subjects, the ocular rotation is mainly determined by otolithic stimulation.
the vestibular system is the main contributor to the perception of the horizontal and that it is mainly the otolith system which is responsible for this function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the visual system is able to generate an ocular counter rotation signal that can be used to stabilize the retinal image.
the ocular counter-rotation is mainly due to vestibular stimulation and not induced by visual stimulation, even if subjects have a loss of vestibular input.
the ocular system can be used as an indicator to assess the contribution of different sensory modalities to the perception of the horizontal in static tilt conditions.
